d.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 2. The Tropical Grassland Region
d.partTitle: Types of Resources and Methods of Exploitation
d.notions: Resource, exploitation, pasture, national park, hydro-electric power, irrigation.
d.focus: Types of resources of the Tropical Grassland region and methods of exploitation.
d.competence: Learners are able to name the resources of the savanna around them and explain how people use them to earn a living.
objectives: Identify the main resources of the Tropical Grassland region.
Describe the methods used to exploit these resources.
recall: The savanna has tall grasses and scattered trees.
Its soils are ferruginous, with laterite and black cotton soils.
Plants survive the dry season by losing leaves and storing water.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: what do families get from the savanna?
situation: Ibrahim lives in a village near the Lagdo lake, south of Garoua. His uncle fishes in the lake, his father grows cotton, and his cousin guides tourists in the Benoue National Park.
A visitor tells Ibrahim that the savanna is a poor region with nothing useful. Ibrahim does not agree, but he cannot explain why.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Ibrahim cannot explain why the savanna is not a poor region with nothing useful.
Which activities do the members of Ibrahim's family practise?
His uncle fishes in the Lagdo lake, his father grows cotton, and his cousin guides tourists in the Benoue National Park.
What can Ibrahim tell the visitor?
He can tell him that the savanna has many resources: land for crops, grass for animals, wildlife, rivers and lakes.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to know the wealth of the savanna where we live and how people use it.

qa.q: Anything in nature that people can use to satisfy their needs is called a ______. What is the missing word?
qa.a: The missing word is resource. Land, water, grass and wild animals are resources.

qa.q: What do we call the action of taking and using a resource for our needs or to earn money?
qa.a: The action of taking and using a resource is called exploitation.

sum.title: I. Definitions
defs: A resource is anything in nature that people can use to satisfy their needs.
Exploitation is the action of taking and using a resource to satisfy needs or to earn money.

qa.q: The savanna has large areas of grass. Which animals can feed on it, and who rears them in North Cameroon?
qa.a: Cattle, sheep and goats feed on the grass. In North Cameroon, the Fulani (Mbororo) herders rear them.

qa.q: Which crops grow well on the soils of the savanna around Garoua?
qa.a: Cotton, maize, sorghum, millet, groundnuts and rice grow well. Cotton is the main cash crop.

qa.q: Name two national parks of North Cameroon. Why are they important resources?
qa.a: The Benoue and Bouba Ndjida National Parks, in the North Region, and Waza, in the Far North, protect wild animals. Tourists visit them.

qa.q: The Lagdo dam was built on the River Benue. Give two ways in which people use its water.
qa.a: The dam produces hydro-electricity (72 MW) for the North. Its lake is used for fishing and for irrigating rice fields.

sum.title: II. Types of Resources and Methods of Exploitation
sum.intro: The main resources of the Tropical Grassland region and their methods of exploitation are the following:
items: A. Pasture
The grass is used to feed cattle, sheep and goats. It is exploited by livestock rearing, as done by the Fulani (Mbororo).
B. Farmland
The soils are used to grow cotton, maize, sorghum, millet and groundnuts. They are exploited by crop farming.
C. Wildlife
Elephants, lions, giraffes and antelopes live in parks such as Benoue, Bouba Ndjida and Waza. They are exploited by tourism and controlled hunting.
D. Water
Rivers and lakes are used for fishing, irrigation and hydro-electricity. The Lagdo dam on the Benue produces 72 MW.
E. Trees
Trees give firewood, charcoal, shea butter and fruits. They are exploited by gathering and cutting.

evaluation: Give two resources of the Tropical Grassland region.
Two resources of the Tropical Grassland region are pasture and wildlife.
How is the water of the Lagdo dam exploited?
It is exploited to produce hydro-electricity, to fish and to irrigate rice fields.
Why are the national parks of North Cameroon important for the economy?
They attract tourists, who spend money on guides, transport and hotels.
remediation: Anything in nature that people can use is a ______.
The action of taking and using a resource is called ______.
Grass used to feed animals is called ______.
The main cash crop of North Cameroon is ______.
The dam built on the Benue near Garoua is the ______ dam.
A national park in the Far North Region is ______.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. resource 2. exploitation 3. pasture 4. cotton 5. Lagdo 6. Waza
d.homework: Ask a farmer or a herder in your area about his work: what he produces, which tools he uses and where he sells his products.

Lagdo dam: on the Benue, south of Garoua, commissioned in the early 1980s, capacity 72 MW.
